questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was mainly to experience a new culture, living in a new city, trying to go to a different university and then of course also that the city is nice and the weather is good

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, they have websites with all the information but not all of the information is in english. Their website can be a bit confusing but if you spend some time on it, you can figure it out

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. We had a welcome session in the start right when we got there, but it was very chaotic because there was problems with capacity on the courses and the person was not the best in english

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very chaotic and confusing in the start, but it will work out good in the end. That is just how it is in Spain

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did it through BCUHousing which has an agreement the university. Maybe I overpayed a little bit compared to other people's housing I saw, but then I was sure that it was not scam

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can find it on your own also, but be careful about scam. It is a little expensive but that is just how it is

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very messy in the start because I needed to take 3 master courses at the Math and Computer Science department and they said in the start that there would not be capacity on the ones I wanted on the Data Science master. Then I thought I had to take advanced math courses but in the end it worked out

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was only one guy helping (the internation coordinator) and he was very slow at answering because he had to help all exchange students at the faculty. I recommend going to his office in person and ask for help because then you get the help straight away

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the courses I wanted so that was good

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can feel very chaotic but it will work out in the end. It is just the Spanish mentality, there is not as much structure as in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
On the math and computer science faculty, the level was high and about what I am used to at KU
At the economic faculty, the level was lower but I also took bachelor level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more classroom teaching, especially at the math and computer science, a bit like we are used to in Gymnasium in Denmark

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Math and Computer Science faculty: Optimization, Machine Learning and Numerical Linear Algebra (all of them on the Data Science Master)
Economic faculty: International Economics and Econometrics I

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Machine Learning and International Economics I liked, especially because of the professors

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food, restaurants, coffee, beers and stuff like that is very cheap here so enjoy that
FC Barcelona tickets were quite expensive, but still good experience (Visca el Barca)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I did a 2 week Catalan course when I arrived before university, that is a good way of meeting international students
Also you can join running clubs, language clubs and a lot of things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Erasmus does a lot of events, so go to some of them. 
Beach volley tournament and some of the trips they did are very good

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the beach, go to a FC Barcelona game and go to some cool cities around Barcelona, there are many good beaches or hiking possibilities and you can use the public transport for free if you get a T-jove card which is like 40€ for three months

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, they are all very nice and kind here

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask about the city and their culture, learn some Catalan/Spanish

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are very relaxed, chill and just enjoy the life and sometimes there is not as much structure and control over everything like in Denmark but you get used to it :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are very kind, open and happy and then of course the good weather

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join the A1 Catalan language course to meet new people, go on trips when you have time either through the Erasmus events or plan them yourself and then if you are having trouble with something it will work out in the end, they are sometimes just a bit slow with it :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really more than what i already wrote

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the spanish culture, living in Barcelona and meeting a lot of cool people from around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit hard being alone in a big city so say yes to a lot of stuff in the beginning and then you will find some people that you connect with and can do stuff together with

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just enjoy it because the time will go fast

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
